correctness.rationale: Exactly three normal scalar measurements give a full-rank design precisely at noninteger middle times; nuisance elimination yields the exact parallax Cramer–Rao variance. Universal contrast/noise bounds establish the unique odd midpoint; phase folding and a unique crossing of a strictly decreasing cotangent term with a strictly increasing rational term prove both and only both even global optima. Explicit determinant comparison and a rigorous expansion prove the criterion mismatch, parity loss, monotonicity and limits. Replayed standalone verifier passed 124806 deterministic assertions; finite numerics are corroboration, not substitutes for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact fixed-integer-baseline marginal-parallax-variance optimizer, odd/even uniqueness classification and parity-dependent incompatibility with saturated full-determinant optimality were not stated or logically implied by the specific published results inspected. Riess et al. use phase-extremal observations with five epochs and additional registration parameters; Michalik et al. study a different five-parameter Bayesian problem; AllWISE reports empirical annual-phase degeneracies. Searches of the semantic mathematical finding index and published astrometric design descriptions returned no equivalent theorem. The risk that a broader classical c-optimal design result could encompass it remains explicitly acknowledged; searched absence is not proof of historical firstness.
residual_risks: Broad pre-2014 c-optimal harmonic-regression literature could imply the theorem without mentioning astrometry or integer years; not all classical design monographs were available for substantive full-text inspection.
Only selected relevant portions of two arXiv papers were inspected, not independently validated complete coverage of every supplemental/appendix result.
The 2013 broad design-method publication was only abstract-level accessible and cannot be certified NOT_COVERING as a whole; a general theorem could conceivably dominate the special case.
The idealized known-cosine scalar model is too restrictive to support operational conclusions for real space telescopes.

value.rationale: The exact object is a natural parsimonious astrometric design where separating parallax from unknown proper motion is intrinsic, and pinned endpoint phases naturally arise from calendar-aligned visits. The proved parity loss says more total years can strictly degrade the best available scalar parallax precision with only three epochs, and reveals a rigorous conflict between scientific-target variance and joint-estimation determinant optimization. The impossibility of identifying parallax at the even midpoint is substantial relative to the nonzero fine optimum; the bounded ~0.12% design adjustment for K=2 is acknowledged rather than exaggerated as a field-practice gain. This is an exact structural classification, not a routine substitution or a claim of observational improvement.
